Casanova’s introspection is closely tied to visible action: his mounting restlessness prompts his abrupt return toward town, while memories of former wealth intensify his anger and shape his encounter with the passing woman. Homesickness, hope, humiliation, rage, and briefly revived vanity form a varied, believable emotional progression. Although introspection dominates, the physical details and unfolding encounter keep it grounded and moving.
